D015-D005_h001.question:
For a little over a year now, it feels like I’ve been walking around with a weight on my chest that never lets up. I get up at 4 a.m. for the toll booth, but it’s on autopilot. I used to crochet on my breaks and watch game shows after work; now I just sit there staring, no interest in anything. Even my kids complain I sound flat on the phone.

My head feels foggy. I keep misplacing money trays or forgetting which cars I’ve already counted. It scares me because I used to be sharp with numbers. Most days, I catch myself thinking it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up, or wishing a truck would just hit my booth so I wouldn’t have to deal with any of this. I don’t have a plan, but those thoughts circle all the time.

In the past year, I’ve started feeling like certain drivers are “sending me messages” with how they look at me or tap their brakes, like it’s about me somehow. Sometimes I feel things crawling on my arms or neck when there’s nothing there. All of that only started after I got this low and has only happened during this long stretch of feeling depressed.
D015-D005_h001.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D015-D005_h001.answer: B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015-D005_h002.question:

Lately I keep thinking it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up. I’m not planning anything, but the thought of just not being here crosses my mind a lot.

On top of that, I’m convinced something’s wrong inside my body, like my organs are rotting, even though tests keep coming back normal. Sometimes when I’m alone in the cab, I smell this strong odor, like something dead or rotten inside me, but no one else can smell it. Those smells and these ideas only started after I got this low and only happen when I’m in this dark mood.
D015-D005_h002.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D015-D005_h002.answer: B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015-D005_h003.question:

These things only started after this long stretch of feeling empty and haven’t happened outside of it.

A. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D015-D005_h004.question:

Those voices and that belief only started after I sank into this depression, and they’ve never shown up outside of it; they seem tied to this whole miserable episode.

A. Persistent Depressive Disorder

    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa

D015-D005_h022.question:
I’ve been really down for a long time now… about eight months. I cry at the smallest things, even at work when I’m mopping the halls and someone just says “good morning.” I try to hide it, but I can’t always stop the tears.

My sleep is all messed up. I fall asleep okay, but I keep waking up in the middle of the night, two, three times, and then I just lie there thinking. I end up going to the kitchen and eating leftovers or making sandwiches. I’m eating way more than I used to, even when I’m not really hungry, and I’ve put on some weight.

I feel like everything bad is my fault—if a light bulb burns out at the building, I think it’s because I didn’t check it enough. If my wife seems tired, I’m sure I’ve ruined her life somehow. I feel like I deserve to be punished.

Lately, I’ve become convinced she’s cheating on me, even though I’ve never seen anything concrete. Sometimes I even see a man standing behind her in our living room, but when I blink, he’s gone. These things—those thoughts and seeing that man—only started after I got this low and only happen when I’m in this dark mood. Before all this, I never saw or believed things like that.
D015-D005_h022.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder
D015-D005_h022.answer: C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015-D005_h023.question:
For about eight months now, it feels like something in me has gone numb. Off camera I feel hollow, like I’m just moving my mouth but there’s nobody inside. I used to love the buzz of the newsroom, the live hits, the makeup chair gossip. Now I sit in my dressing room between segments and stare at the wall, feeling nothing, or this dull, heavy ache.

My sleep is strange. I fall asleep exhausted but wake up around 3 or 4 a.m. every night, wide awake, mind spinning, and I can’t get back to sleep. I end up eating mindlessly in the kitchen, and my clothes are noticeably tighter — I’ve put on quite a bit of weight just in the past month.

The guilt is…extreme. I’m convinced that bad things I read on the teleprompter — a plane crash, a shooting — are somehow my fault, like I caused them by reporting them or even thinking about them. I know that doesn’t make sense, but it feels absolutely true.

Lately, during this same period, I sometimes see people standing at the edge of the studio who aren’t actually there. And I’m certain a famous politician I report on is secretly in love with me, sending me messages through his speeches. These things only started after I sank into this low mood and have never happened outside of it.
D015-D005_h023.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder
D015-D005_h023.answer: C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015-D005_h024.question:
For about eight months now I’ve just been…down. It’s like this heavy gray filter over everything. I cry at the smallest things—editing footage, a commercial, even just looking at my son’s photo. It’s embarrassing; I used to be composed on set, and now I tear up in meetings.

Nights are the worst. I lie in bed staring at the ceiling for hours, replaying every mistake I’ve ever made. I’m exhausted but can’t fall asleep. I’ve also pretty much stopped eating—food tastes like cardboard, and I have to force down a few bites just so I don’t pass out on shoots. I’ve lost a lot of weight.

I can’t shake this certainty that I’ve caused horrible things to happen—like I’m somehow responsible for disasters I see on the news, that my films set off a chain of events. I know it sounds irrational, but it feels absolutely true.

Lately I’m convinced something is rotting inside me, like my organs are decaying, even though tests came back normal. And when my mood is at its darkest, I sometimes see shadowy figures in the corner of my room or on location—people no one else sees. These things only happen when I’m in this deep low; there aren’t any strange experiences outside of that. It’s gotten to the point where I can barely work or take care of myself.
D015-D005_h024.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder
D015-D005_h024.answer: C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015-D005_h025.question:
It’s been about eight months now that I’ve felt…flat, low, almost constantly. I drag myself to the branch every day, but I’m just going through the motions. I used to really care about my numbers, my team; now I feel like a complete failure, like everyone would be better off if they had a different manager, a different husband, a different dad. I keep thinking I’m useless, that I’ve somehow ruined everything.

My sleep is awful. I wake up from these graphic, terrifying dreams most nights—people getting hurt, my family dying, or me being humiliated at work. After that, it’s hard to get back to sleep, so I end up eating in the kitchen at 3 a.m. I’ve put on a lot of weight over just a few weeks, my suits barely fit.

Lately, during this low period, I’ve been convinced that one of the senior executives at head office is secretly in love with me—like her emails have hidden meanings. At the same time, I’ll suddenly get this strong metallic, almost rotten taste in my mouth when there’s nothing there. Those things only started after I got this depressed; when I’ve had brief moments of feeling a bit better, they fade too.
D015-D005_h025.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder
D015-D005_h025.answer: C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
